summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to accelerate AI development for skin image analysis for dermatology applications using pre-trained embeddings. It produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output, useful for downstream tasks.
keywords: machine learning; dermatology; image analysis; embeddings; skin conditions; classification
intended_use_and_workflow: Derm Foundation reduces the data, compute, and expertise needed to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis. Embeddings can be used for classifying conditions, scoring severity, identifying body parts, and determining image quality.
primary_intended_users: Businesses and institutions in healthcare and life sciences
how_to_use: Use code snippets to run the model locally. For large-scale use, create a production version using Model Garden.
model_limitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting or noise conditions. It was trained on data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and may not generalize well to other countries or patient populations. It generates embeddings only.
outcomes_and_output: Produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output
type_and_value_of_solution_output: Embedding vector of floating point values (Dimensions: 6144)
explanation_for_how_an_output_is_generat: Derm Foundation is pre-trained on large amounts of labeled skin images to produce 6144 dimensional embeddings that capture dense features relevant for analyzing these images.
input_data_source: A large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web and tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images.
development_data_characterization: Derm Foundation was trained in two stages. The first pre-training stage used contrastive learning to train on a large number of public image-text pairs from the internet. The image component of this pre-trained model was then fine-tuned for condition classification and a couple other downstream tasks using clinical datasets.
training_data: Derm Foundation's base model was pre-trained using a large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web. The supervised fine-tuned model used tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images [SOURCE 1].
demographic_representativeness: The supervised fine-tuned model was trained using data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and settings (mostly clinical). It may not generalize well to data from other countries, patient populations, or image types not used in training [SOURCE 1].
usefulness_efficacy_goal_of_metrics: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks [SOURCE 1]. The goal is to reduce the training data, compute, and technical expertise necessary to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis [SOURCE 1].
usefulness_efficacy_result: Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundations embeddings were substantially more performant (10-15% increase in accuracy) than doing the same for a standard BiT-M model across different proportions of training data [SOURCE 1]. Models built on top of the Derm Foundation embeddings for dermatology-related tasks achieved significantly higher quality than those built solely on embeddings or fine tuned from BiT-M, particularly when working with smaller training datasets [SOURCE 4].
usefulness_efficacy_interpretation: The results demonstrate that the Derm Foundation tool can serve as a useful starting point to accelerate skin-related modeling tasks [SOURCE 4].
usefulness_efficacy_test_type: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks [SOURCE 1]. The modeling variants considered were a linear classifier on frozen embeddings from BiT-M, a fine-tuned version of BiT-M, a linear classifier on frozen embeddings from the Derm Foundation API, and a fine-tuned version of the model underlying the Derm Foundation API [SOURCE 4].
usefulness_efficacy_testing_data_descrip: The SFT (supervised fine-tuned) model was trained data from a limited set of countries (United States, Colombia, Australia, public images) and settings (mostly clinical). [SOURCE 1]
usefulness_efficacy_validation_process_a: Downstream models built using Derm Foundation still require careful evaluation to understand their expected performance in the intended setting [SOURCE 4].
